scope: Disposable local Herdr agents and loopback SSH transport; no production bridge or iOS timeline

results.finding: Stock SessionStart integration reports a native ID. Exact-ID resume and cross-workspace pane move retain it; concurrent same-cwd agents have distinct IDs; replacing an occupant changes the ID while retaining terminal ID.
Captured native JSONL user/assistant messages, Read tool call/result, AskUserQuestion, and user interruption. Metadata and hook attachments also occur; adapters must filter intentionally.

Stock integration reports IDs after starting a thread in --no-daemon mode with inherited CODEX_THREAD_ID cleared. Distinct same-cwd sessions, exact-ID resume and cross-workspace move are verified. SessionStart can occur when the first thread is created, later than the initial TUI idle screen.

The default shared-daemon test launch did not provide agent_session, even after its completed turn. Clearing the TUI shell's inherited thread ID was insufficient in this run. Do not guess the thread by cwd or choose the newest history. Root cause and daemon launch-context propagation need a separate investigation.

Installed Codex uses paginated history. state_5.sqlite identifies history_mode and rollout_path; thread_history_1.sqlite stores typed items, turns and update ordinals. A legacy JSONL rollout also exists, but its availability alone is not a verified full-history contract. Compare a supported history read API with version-gated read-only database access before selecting the production adapter.

events.subscribe acknowledges and emits workspace events. Keep its socket separate from command requests; attempting a second request on the subscribed socket closed the stream in this experiment. Closing the subscription leaves the server healthy. Snapshot is a separate read. Event envelopes have no global sequence/replay cursor in protocol 22.

Disposable localhost-only OpenSSH server with pinned host key and temporary public-key authentication passed incremental Unicode output, stdin echo, cancellation, and subsequent reconnection. This is transport evidence, not a live Citadel/iOS bridge test.

withExec exposes bidirectional non-PTY streams and closes the channel on closure completion/error. Herdcats already uses it in PanePersistentShell. A live mobile stream and idle-read cancellation still need tests during bridge integration.

Current saved-machine routing executes buffered Herdr CLI commands on the gateway. It does not expose a generic child-host bidirectional bridge stream. Keep routed timelines disabled until explicit forwarding and ownership tests exist.

No dedicated pending approval/question response method is exposed in the captured request schema. A blocked status and historical transcript tool call do not supply a live request-specific acknowledgement path. The harmless question was canceled through the terminal; no real operation was approved.

A sanitized captured record was used to construct split-UTF8 and missing-newline cases, an unknown record, and actual rename/replace and truncate operations on a temporary copy. These are reproducible adapter inputs, not naturally observed agent rotation or a production follower test.

next_phase.recommended: Build the read-only bridge foundation with Claude first and independently gate Codex support by exact native session identity and verified history access.
next_phase.claude: Proven identity source and JSONL shapes permit a fixture-backed adapter prototype. Resolve ID to the exact transcript by verified session metadata/index; never by newest cwd entry.
next_phase.codex: Local-process identity proven. Finalize paginated history reading and investigate daemon context before claiming general Codex support. Do not silently change a user's launch mode.
next_phase.transport: Direct SSH stream first; verify Citadel live cancellation and generation ownership. Saved remote machine streams remain capability-disabled.
next_phase.actions: Read-only request display only. Native responses remain false capabilities until a live, request-bound integration is proven.

verification.ios_tests: not rerun; production iOS source unchanged

fixture_policy: Only disposable sessions were captured. Free text is replaced, IDs pseudonymized, paths replaced, and account/global instruction fields omitted. Sanitized fixtures preserve relevant source shape and relational links. The sanitizer is a fixture aid, not a general-purpose guarantee for arbitrary private logs.
report_storage: report.json is the versionable report. Markdown and Lavish summaries stay local according to repository ignore rules. No commit or push was performed.
